TWO QUEUE-LAYER CONSEQUENCES OF THE DIAL THAT PASS 2 DOES NOT STATE, and that a build following pass 2 alone would get wrong. (1) SPACING MUST NOT STALL THE ITERATION (Q-APP-5, arm A9): if the top candidate's family is inside its spacing window the iteration falls through the order and fires the first candidate whose family is not. Otherwise one family at appetite_effective = 1 holds the WHOLE fleet at its own spacing_max -- pass 2 §4.2's `max(1, ...)` prevents a dial from being a silent off at the family level, and this prevents the identical failure one layer up. This admits the layer's only clock into a dispatch path (design §9 argues against clocks there); it is narrowed to a per-family rate limit that can never decide WHICH row runs, the new state is one `last_dispatch_at` per family (§11), and §13 OQ 9 offers the operator the alternative of dropping spacing entirely -- which would be a pass-2 amendment, not a local choice. (2) A ROW SKIPPED ON LANES OR SPACING STAYS ELIGIBLE AND ACCRUES age, while a row a DIAL forbids does not and can never anchor (Q-CAP-3) -- the transient/permanent distinction is what keeps the self-DoS hole shut under the dial.

MECHANISM GAP FOUND WHILE COMMITTING (worth a row; it will bite every author-fix row). The pre-commit hook refused the spec commit: 'staged paths outside the scope of task T576'. The cause is not a mistake in the row — `bin/managent show T576` reports holds=docs/epics/E1-markovian/L1-dashboard/S03-queue-layer/spec.md, i.e. the kanban records this row as that file's single writer — but `tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh scope` derives commit permission from the bundle's `deliverables=` header ∪ findings/<id>-*.json ∪ four coordination surfaces, and **never reads `holds`**. So `holds` grants the write and denies the commit. The two fields are used by the same lib for opposite purposes: `active-holders` reads holds ∪ deliverables (conflict detection), `scope` reads deliverables only (commit permission). For a mutation row whose product IS the held file and whose only declared deliverable is a findings file — which is the shape of every author-fix and every spec-revision row — the mechanism is structurally unable to let the work land. This row committed via `tools/git-commit-mine --explicit`, the sanctioned take-responsibility mode, naming exactly the two paths (the held spec and the findings file); the real hazard the wrapper exists to stop (sweeping another console's staged work from the shared index) is fully guarded either way, since --explicit still stages ONLY the named paths. tools/git-commit-mine-lib.sh was deliberately NOT edited: widening one's own commit scope is exactly the change that needs a different writer, and this row holds only the spec. Recommended fix for whoever owns the lib: make `scope` = deliverables ∪ holds ∪ findings/<id>-* ∪ the four surfaces. holds is already the repo's single-writer assertion, and a file a row may write is a file that row must be able to commit — anything else forces --explicit as routine, which is how a guard becomes noise (`project-process-doctrine`: fix the tool, do not add prose).
